_meta.indication: SUTENT is indicated for the treatment of gastrointestinal stromal tumor after disease progression on or intolerance to imatinib mesylate.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study A6181004 (also referred to as Study A)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled international Phase 3 trial in 56 centers, with patients randomized 2:1 to sunitinib or placebo plus best supportive care
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who were intolerant of or who had disease progression during prior imatinib treatment
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to tumor progression (TTP), time from randomization to first documentation of objective tumor progression
pivotal_trials.result: At planned interim analysis after 149 TTP events, median TTP 27.3 weeks (SUTENT) vs 6.4 weeks (placebo), HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.23, 0.47), p<0.0001

key_safety: In GIST Study A, Grade 3/4 treatment-emergent AEs occurred in 56% (SUTENT) vs 51% (placebo). Common AEs (SUTENT vs placebo) included fatigue (42% vs 47%), diarrhea (40% vs 27%), nausea (31% vs 32%), and mucositis/stomatitis (29% vs 18%); decreased LVEF was increased on SUTENT (11%) vs placebo (3%)
target_moa: Small-molecule oral multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor that blocks signaling via multiple RTKs including VEGFR, PDGFR, KIT and FLT-3

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed at an advisory committee meeting

basis.text: Priority designation (P); the application was given Priority consideration and classified as a new molecular entity (NME)

summary.text: NDA 21-938 for GIST received Priority review as an NME and was granted regular (full) approval on January 26, 2006, based on the primary endpoint of time to tumor progression from the randomized Phase 3 Study A6181004; TTP had been accepted as supporting regular approval for GIST following imatinib progression.

citations.quote: The Division of Drug Oncology Products (DDOP), OODP, CDER, FDA recommends that FDA approve SUTENT via the regular approval mechanism for treatment of gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after progression on or intolerance to imatinib mesylate.

NDA 21-938 for the treatment of gastrointestinal stromal tumor after disease progression on or intolerance to imatinib mesylate is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling text.
TTP was accepted as an endpoint supporting regular approval of Sutent for treatment of malignant GIST following progression on imatinib, dependent on magnitude of benefit and conduct
